A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing new catalysts to convert propane to acrylic acid and we are developing new reactors to make acrylic acid.
the catalysts were able to convert propane into acrylonitrile with a high selectivity, while maintaining a reasonable conversion of propane to acrylonitriles.
it is possible to obtain high yields of acrylic acid from propane oxidation using catalysts containing molybdenum, vanadium and tellurium in the presence of a hydrogen halide, such as HCl.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of an inorganic catalyst is not only feasible, but can also be more effective than the use of organic catalysts.
we have shown that the MoO3-V2O5-TeO2 catalyst is an active catalyst for the gas-phase propane oxidation reaction, and that it is a potential catalyst for the production of acrylic acid.
